title: の (possession; modification)
meaning: "of / 's" — links two nouns: possession, attribute, origin, or apposition. Also a pronoun "one".
simpleExplanation: の links two nouns so that the first one describes the second: 私の傘 "my umbrella", 日本語の先生 "a teacher of Japanese", 東京の大学 "a university in Tokyo". The word before の always describes the word after it, so the order is the opposite of English "of". の can also stand in for a noun you already mentioned: 赤いの "the red one".
whenUsed: Ownership (my, your, Tanaka's), what something is made of or about, where something is from (日本の車), and replacing a repeated noun ("the red one"). Extremely frequent; N5 reading passages are full of の chains like 私の友達の家.
formation: い-adjective + の  (赤いの = the red one)
Noun + の  (これは私のです = this is mine)

examples.reading: これは わたしの かさです。

examples.ja: 日本語の先生はどこですか。
examples.reading: にほんごの せんせいは どこですか。
examples.note: "Teacher of Japanese": the first noun says what kind of teacher.

examples.reading: あかいのを ください。
examples.en: Please give me the red one.
examples.note: の as a pronoun: "the red one" (no need to repeat 傘).

examples.reading: あれは にほんの くるまです。
examples.note: Origin: 日本の車 = a car from Japan. 車の日本 would mean something else entirely.

examples.ja: このかばんは田中さんのです。
examples.reading: この かばんは たなかさんのです。
examples.note: Noun + の with no following noun = "Tanaka's (one)".

similarGrammar.difference: な-adjectives use な, not の, before a noun: 静かな町 (not 静かの町).
A different の: at the end of a sentence it gives an explanation.
と joins two equal nouns (A and B); の makes one noun describe the other.

commonMistakes.why: The describing word comes first. 日本の車 = a car (that is) from Japan.
な-adjectives take な before a noun, not の.
い-adjectives go straight onto the noun. Use 赤いの only when the noun is left out ("the red one").

usageNotes: In casual speech の can end a question (行くの？). The first noun modifies the second — 日本の車 "Japanese car", 車の日本 is wrong.
jlptTips: Between two nouns, の is almost always the answer. The trap is when the first word is a な-adjective (静か, 有名, きれい): then it is な.
In 〜のです／〜のですか, the の is the explanatory ending, not possession; do not be confused when the blank comes right before です.
